newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PICOP to increase capital, split stock.
newsitem.headline: PICOP to increase capital, split stock.

text.p: PICOP Resources Inc said on Thursday its shareholders had agreed to an increase in the company's authorised capital stock.
They also approved a plan to split each share into five shares and amend the par value of the shares to one peso per share from five pesos.
Analysts said this was intended to make PICOP shares more affordable.
The company said earlier it wanted to raise its authorised capital stock to 10 billion pesos from 6.0 billion.

PICOP Resources, the country's largest industrial timber firm, reported a net loss of 718.6 million pesos in the first half of 1996, which included a one-time provision for a restructuring cost of 611.8 million pesos.
PICOP also cited weak market conditions and higher bunker fuel prices for its lacklustre earnings performance.

"To achieve a stronger foundation, a company-wide organisational restructuring programme is being implemented to establish a lean, cost-effective, focused organisation where only the core businesses of the company will remain," PICOP chairman Ramon Montano said in a statement.
A new management team took over PICOP in July. Guoco Holdings Philippines Inc sold its stake in PICOP Resources to local cement maker Far East Cement Corp.
